title: Cross-session lock test does not detect global serialization
reasoning: This test claims to prove independent session locks do not block each other, but the two signOut operations are immediate stubbed operations and the measured elapsed time is intentionally unused. A production regression to one global session lock would still run both sign-outs sequentially and almost certainly complete within the one-minute suite limit, so the test would pass while the intended concurrency guarantee is broken.
recommendation: Make one session operation hold its lock behind a deterministic gate while starting an operation for another session, then assert the second session completes before releasing the first gate. Avoid relying on broad suite timeout as proof of concurrency.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only verifies both sessions eventually sign out; it has no assertion that session s2 can progress while session s1 is blocked.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that starts a gated signOut/refresh for s1, waits until it has entered the locked section, starts signOut for s2, asserts s2 completes within a short deterministic timeout, then releases s1 and awaits completion.
minimumFixScope: Update SessionLockTests.differentSessionsDontBlockEachOther to include a deterministic blocking stub or test hook and a completion-order assertion.
